Alastair Campbell:
Nobody has won the Legs Open with a lower score than Alastair Campbell. Four under par nett at Carnwath in 2013, the very first championship, and thirteen editions later it still stands. Kevin Park came closest, three under at St Andrews in 2020.

That opening day was nearly a clean sweep. His 75 was the best gross in the field, which brought the Scratch title along with the Main, and his 40 Stableford points topped the lot. Only Bobby Ferguson, in the same year, has matched that tally. The one thing that stopped Campbell holding all three trophies was the rule that keeps the Main champion out of the Stableford.

He came back to finish tied second at Lanark in 2015 and tied sixth at Blairgowrie in 2021, five championships in all between 2013 and 2021.
David Clee:
David Clee is one of only two men to have won the Legs Open twice, and he did it in consecutive years. Andrew Duncan is the only one to have defended the title since. You would struggle to find two wins less alike.

The first came at Lanark in 2015, at four over par. The second, at Southerness in 2016, came at seventeen over, the highest winning score in the championship's history by a distance, and a fair summary of the weather that day. His gross 101 took the Scratch as well.

Twelve appearances between 2013 and 2026 have made him one of the fixtures of the field, and rarely a passenger. Tied third on debut in 2013, fourth at Gullane in 2018, fifth at Ladybank in 2019 and fifth again at Balmedie in 2025. Over the same stretch his handicap has tumbled from 17 to 6.
Andrew Duncan:
Andrew Duncan joined David Clee as the only men to have defended the Legs Open, a decade after Clee did it. Level par at Downfield in 2024, level par again at Balmedie in 2025, and the second of those rounded off with a 75, the best gross of the day, for the Scratch title too.

It had been coming. He finished second on debut at Ladybank in 2019 and won the Stableford there with 35 points, then went fourth at St Andrews in 2020 and tied second at Loch Lomond in 2022.

Across his seven appearances the handicap has fallen from 12 to 1, which makes those two level-par nett rounds a good deal harder earned at the end than they would have been at the start.
Colin Howieson:
Colin Howieson won the Legs Open at Dalmahoy in 2017 at two over par, and picked up the Scratch on the same afternoon with a gross 79.

A second title very nearly followed at Panmure in 2023, where he tied for the lead on one over and lost on the countback. He had the Stableford for consolation, 35 points, and a 78 that remains the best round he has played in the championship.

His eight appearances have been stop-start affairs. Four have ended without a card, three of them in the last five. When he does get round, though, he is rarely far from the top.
Bryan Forbes:
Bryan Forbes won at Ladybank in 2019 at one under par. Only four championships in fourteen have been won under par, and his is one of them.

It was a thorough day's work. His 79, still his lowest round, took the Scratch, and his 38 points led the Stableford. Only four totals in the championship's history have been better.

He has not missed one since, eight in a row from 2019 to 2026, with a fifth at St Andrews in 2020 and a pair of tied ninths at Loch Lomond in 2022 and Castle Stuart in 2026.
Kevin Park:
Kevin Park won at St Andrews in 2020 at three under par, the second-lowest winning score the Legs Open has produced.

He topped the Stableford that day too, with 39 points. Only Alastair Campbell and Bobby Ferguson have beaten that, and both did it back in 2013. Fourth at Ladybank the year before and tied seventh at Balmedie in 2025 are the nearest he has come since.

Over eight appearances his handicap has come down from 26 to 15, and at 64 he is among the oldest men to have lifted the trophy.
Nick Ward:
Nick Ward won the Legs Open at the first attempt, at Blairgowrie in 2021, two under par.

His gross 80 took the Scratch in the same round, and his 38 Stableford points would have won that too had the rules allowed the Main champion to keep it. Only two men have ever won the championship with a lower score.

He has played twice since, finishing 12th at Loch Lomond in 2022 and 16th at Downfield in 2024.
Lloyd Swan:
Lloyd Swan turned up at Loch Lomond in 2022 for his first Legs Open and won it, a level-par nett 72 that left a four-way tie two shots behind him.

His 36 Stableford points were the best in the field and his gross 82 was fifth. He came back to Panmure the following year, finished fifth, and has not played since.
Barry Thomas:
Barry Thomas won at Panmure in 2023 on one over par, after a tie at the top with Colin Howieson went to the countback. Over the first, second, seventeenth and eighteenth he was two under and Howieson one over, and that settled it.

He had the best Stableford score that day as well, 35 points, but the Main title came first and the Stableford went to Howieson.

Three appearances in all: a no-return at St Andrews in 2020, the title in 2023, and 27th at Downfield in 2024.
David Burns:
David Burns won the Legs Open at Gullane in 2018 at two over par, and his 34 points led the Stableford in the same round.

It was the third of four appearances in five years. He had been ninth at Lanark in 2015 and fourth at Dalmahoy in 2017, and came back in 2019 to finish tenth at Ladybank.
John Pow:
John Pow won at Dundonald Links in 2014 at two over par, with 34 points to lead the Stableford.

The year before at Carnwath he had finished fifth, one under, and his gross 81 was second only to the champion's. Those are his only two appearances, and at 70 he remains the oldest man to have won the championship.
Steven Leisegang:
Steven Leisegang won at Castle Stuart in 2026 on his only appearance, and he did it the hard way. A seven at the first and another at the second left him five over after two holes.

From there he steadied to a nett 75, three over, and finished two clear of Stevie Connelly. His 33 Stableford points were the best in the field, but with the Main title in hand the Stableford passed to Connelly.

He is the only South African to have played the championship.
Mark Alston:
Mark Alston has never missed one. Fourteen Legs Opens, from Carnwath in 2013 to Castle Stuart in 2026, and only Robert Hamilton can say the same.

He arrived with a flourish, two under and tied third on debut, and matched that finish at Blairgowrie in 2021, this time at level par. The years in between brought a fourth at Southerness in 2016 and a pair of fifths, at Dundonald Links and Gullane.

The handicap tells its own story, down from 24 to 13 over the run. So, less kindly, does the scorecard drawer: three of his last eight championships have ended without a card being returned.
Robert Hamilton:
Robert Hamilton has played all fourteen Legs Opens, and he and Stephen Magowan are the only men to have won the Stableford twice. His came at Lanark in 2015 with 33 points and at Balmedie in 2025 with 34.

Lanark was his finest afternoon. He took the Scratch with an 83 and tied second in the Main. Ten years later at Balmedie he went one better, second on his own at two over.

Add a third at Southerness in 2016 and a fourth at Dundonald Links in 2014. His lowest round is the 82 at Blairgowrie in 2021, which made him runner-up in the Scratch.
Stephen Magowan:
Stephen Magowan has won the Stableford twice, at Gullane in 2018 with 32 points and at St Andrews in 2020 with 33, and in 2020 he took the Scratch as well with an 86.

In both of those years he was runner-up in the Main, four over par each time. Robert Hamilton is the only other man to have finished second twice without going on to win.

Eleven appearances since 2016 make him one of the regulars, and at 60 one of the senior members of the field.
Colum Watters:
Colum Watters has teed it up in eleven Legs Opens since 2016. Only five of them have produced a finished card.

When he gets round, he tends to be in the thick of it. He was third at St Andrews in 2020, five over, and tied second in the Stableford there with 33 points, having finished tied sixth at Ladybank the year before. His 93 at St Andrews is still his best round.

Six no-returns, three of them in his first four appearances, is the most of anyone on the roster.
David Pow:
David Pow has played nine Legs Opens across the fourteen years, from Carnwath in 2013 to Castle Stuart in 2026.

His best finish is seventh at Loch Lomond in 2022, five over par. He was ninth at Dundonald Links in 2014 and eleventh on debut in 2013, when his 104 also came eleventh in the Scratch.

Four of his last six championships have finished without a card, and his handicap has gone in the opposite direction to most of the field, out from 20 to 24.
Toby Stanton:
Toby Stanton is the only Englishman to have played the Legs Open, with seven appearances between 2013 and 2023.

His best returns are sixth on debut at Carnwath in 2013, three over, and tied sixth at Blairgowrie in 2021 at four over. In 2013 he was also sixth in the Stableford with 35 points.

Four of the seven have ended without a card.
Stevie Anderson:
Stevie Anderson has six appearances since 2021, and the pick of them is Panmure in 2023. He finished third there at four over, third in the Stableford on 32 points and tied third in the Scratch with an 82.

Fifth at Blairgowrie in 2021 and sixth at Balmedie in 2025 fill out a steady record, and over the six years his handicap has come down from 13 to 8.
Andrew Spiers:
Andrew Spiers won the Stableford at Blairgowrie in 2021 with 39 points. Only two totals have been better, and one has matched it.

He was second in the Main that day too, one under, a shot behind Nick Ward. It is comfortably his best championship. Eighth at Loch Lomond in 2022 is his only other top-ten finish, and three of his five appearances have ended without a card.
Bobby Ferguson:
Bobby Ferguson played the first two Legs Opens and won the Stableford in the first, with 40 points. Alastair Campbell matched it the same day, and nobody has bettered it since.

He tied Campbell for the Main title at Carnwath on four under before losing the countback, and his 81 was second in the Scratch. He returned in 2014 to finish third at Dundonald Links.
Davie Clelland:
Davie Clelland played twice, in 2014 and 2015, and at Dundonald Links in 2014 he took both the Stableford and the Scratch, with 32 points and a gross 85.

He was runner-up in the Main that day at four over, and came back the following year to finish tied fifth at Lanark.
Bruce Cruickshanks:
Bruce Cruickshanks won the Stableford at Dalmahoy in 2017 with 34 points, on a day when he also tied for the Main title at two over and lost the countback to Colin Howieson.

His 87 was second in the Scratch. Three appearances in three years have been consistent ones, with a sixth at Gullane in 2018 and a tied sixth at Ladybank in 2019 to follow.
Grahame Ingram:
Grahame Ingram played one Legs Open, at Southerness in 2016, and won the Stableford with 22 points.

It was the hardest championship on record, won at seventeen over par. His gross 107 was third in the Scratch and his nett second in the Main. At 71 he is the oldest man to have played.
Scott Ingram:
Scott Ingram won the Stableford at Southerness in 2016, in the championship that produced the highest winning score the event has seen.

He was fifth in the Main that day and fourth in the Scratch. His five appearances span thirteen years, from Carnwath in 2013 to a no-return at Castle Stuart in 2026, with a seventh at Dundonald Links in 2014 and a tied seventh at Lanark in 2015 along the way.
John McAlpine:
John McAlpine won the Stableford at Downfield in 2024 with 37 points, and he did it without returning a card, having picked up at the 14th.

No other no-return has ever won a Legs Open competition. A picked-up hole knocks you out of the Main and the Scratch but only costs you that hole in the Stableford, and his 37 points were still the best in the field.

Four appearances, and every one a no-return. The handicap has come down from 40 to 32 along the way.
Neal Eadie:
Neal Eadie won the Stableford at Loch Lomond in 2022 with 34 points. Four players finished level, and his 19 points on the inward nine beat the other three outright.

He was tied second in the Main that day at two over, and his 77 was second in the Scratch. He came back to Panmure in 2023 for a tied sixth, and has played no others.
Doug Scott:
Doug Scott owns the lowest gross round in Legs Open history, a 74 at Loch Lomond in 2022. It won him the Scratch and left him tied second in the Main.

He plays off the lowest handicaps in the field, scratch in 2022 and plus one by 2023. He has four appearances between 2022 and 2025, and the last two ended without a card.
Tom Sinton:
Tom Sinton won the Scratch at Panmure in 2023 with a 77, and finished fourth in the Main the same day.

The year before at Loch Lomond he had been tied second, two over, with 34 points for a share of second in the Stableford. Four appearances in five years, and at 62 his handicap has come down from 7 to 5.
Andrew Oliphant:
Andrew Oliphant has won the Scratch twice in three appearances, with a 76 at Downfield in 2024 and an 82 at Castle Stuart in 2026, and he has never finished outside the top six in the Main.

He was fourth on debut at two over, tied third at Balmedie in 2025 and sixth in 2026. Playing off two, he is among the lowest handicaps the championship has seen, and that 76 is the fourth-lowest round on record.
George Burns:
George Burns won the Scratch at Gullane in 2018 with an 86, and finished third in the Main that day at five over par.

He had been fifth at Dalmahoy the year before. Three appearances in three years, the last of them a no-return at Ladybank in 2019.
Stevie Connelly:
Stevie Connelly won the Stableford at Castle Stuart in 2026 with 31 points, and finished runner-up in the Main, five over and two behind Steven Leisegang.

That was a big step forward. His three previous appearances had brought two no-returns and a tied seventeenth at Downfield in 2024.
Fraser Donaldson:
Fraser Donaldson was tied second at Downfield in 2024, one over par, and tied second in the Scratch the same day with a 77, still his lowest round.

Off one, he is among the lowest handicaps in the field, which makes the 35 points that earned him a share of third in the Stableford that year an impressive return. Five appearances since 2022, including a sixth at Loch Lomond on debut and a tied seventh at Castle Stuart in 2026.
John Taylor:
John Taylor's Legs Open career comes in two halves. He played the first two championships, at Carnwath and Dundonald Links, finishing seventh and eighth, and then disappeared for a decade.

He has been better since he came back in 2024. Tied fifth at Downfield, tied third at Balmedie in 2025 at six over with 32 points for a share of third in the Stableford, and tied ninth at Castle Stuart. Across the gap his handicap has come down from 18 to 11.
Owen Watters:
Owen Watters finished third at Ladybank in 2019, two over, and his 86 was third in the Scratch. It is his best round and his best championship by some way.

His debut the year before was one of the four cards lost at Gullane, when the closing group's scorecards were ruined by the rain and the digital scoring went down with them. Three of his five appearances have ended without a return. The other produced a tied sixth at Panmure in 2023.
David McGowan:
David McGowan has played five championships in a row since 2022 and finished every one of them, which is more than most of the field can say.

His best is a tied seventh at Balmedie in 2025, nine over par. His 88 at Panmure in 2023, tied eighth in the Scratch on a day he was also tied eighth in the Main, is as close as he has come to a low round.
Jim Yuille:
Jim Yuille finished third at Dalmahoy in 2017, five over, with an 87 that tied for second in the Scratch and 31 points for a share of third in the Stableford. It is comfortably the best of his four appearances.

He had been sixth at Dundonald Links in 2014. The other two, in 2015 and 2020, ended without a card.
Iain MacLeod:
Iain MacLeod played four of the first five Legs Opens, finishing eighth at Carnwath in 2013 and tenth at Dundonald Links the following year.

His best Stableford came last, a share of third at Dalmahoy in 2017 with 31 points, alongside a tied eighth in the Main.
Martin McErlean:
Martin McErlean finished tied third at Blairgowrie in 2021 on debut, level par, and was second in the Stableford with 38 points. Only four men have bettered that.

He was playing off 42 at the time, the second-highest handicap the championship has recorded behind John McAlpine's 46. It has since come down to 29, but his three appearances since that debut have all ended without a card.
Mark Kennedy:
Mark Kennedy has four appearances since 2023, and three of them ended without a card.

The exception was Balmedie in 2025, where he finished tied fourteenth at twelve over with a 92, twelfth in the Scratch.
Colin Hart:
Colin Hart has got better every year. Tied fourteenth at Downfield in 2024, tied seventh at Balmedie in 2025, and tied fourth at Castle Stuart in 2026 at seven over par.

In 2025 he took a share of third in the Stableford with 32 points, and across the three years his handicap has come down from 16 to 12.
Ross Dick:
Ross Dick was tied fifth on debut at Downfield in 2024, three over, with an 84 for sixth in the Scratch and 33 points for a share of sixth in the Stableford.

At 26 he is the youngest man on the roster, and his handicap has dropped sharply from 9 to 4 over three appearances. A tied tenth at Balmedie followed in 2025.
Brian McGuire:
Brian McGuire has finished all three of his championships and moved up each time, from tied ninth at Downfield in 2024 to tied seventh at Castle Stuart in 2026, ten over par.

His 86 at Downfield is his lowest round, and his handicap has come down from 9 to 6 in three years.
Ross McCallum:
Ross McCallum was tied ninth on debut at Downfield in 2024, five over, with 33 points for a share of sixth in the Stableford.

A no-return at Balmedie followed the next year, and he was tied eighteenth at Castle Stuart in 2026.
Michael Holton:
Michael Holton finished tied tenth at Panmure in 2023 on debut and tied fourteenth at Downfield the following year, where his 85 was seventh in the Scratch and remains his lowest round.

His third appearance, at Balmedie in 2025, ended without a card.
Gary Drummond:
Gary Drummond was tied ninth on debut at Downfield in 2024, five over, and his 79 was fourth in the Scratch. Only thirteen rounds under 80 have ever been returned in the championship, and that is one of them.

He plays off plus one, among the lowest handicaps in the field. Both his appearances since have ended without a card.
Cameron Dyer: Cameron Dyer is, at 27, one of the three youngest men on the roster. His debut at Downfield in 2024 ended without a card, but he has finished both championships since, tied twelfth at Balmedie in 2025 at eleven over and twenty-third at Castle Stuart in 2026.
Grant Robertson:
Grant Robertson has three appearances since 2023, and two of them ended without a card.

The exception was Castle Stuart in 2026, where he finished tied eighteenth at sixteen over with a 93, fourteenth in the Scratch.
Ross Findlay:
Ross Findlay has played the last three championships and finished all three, the best of them twenty-first at Balmedie in 2025.

At 27 he is among the youngest in the field, and his handicap has come down from 7 to 5 over the three years.
Stuart Hamilton:
Stuart Hamilton was tied second on debut at Downfield in 2024, one over par, and off 20 he took a share of third in the Stableford with 35 points.

He came back to Balmedie the following year and finished twentieth, and has played no others.
Chris Peffers:
Chris Peffers finished tied ninth on debut at Loch Lomond in 2022, seven over, with an 87 that was eighth in the Scratch.

He came back at Downfield in 2024 for a tied seventeenth.
Gerard Doyle:
Gerard Doyle was tied ninth on debut at Downfield in 2024, five over, with 33 points for a share of sixth in the Stableford and an 88 for a share of twelfth in the Scratch.

His second appearance, at Balmedie in 2025, ended without a card.
Keiran Dougan:
Keiran Dougan finished eighth at Downfield in 2024, four over par, off 27. Nobody else in that year's top ten played off a higher handicap.

His debut at Panmure the year before had ended without a card, though his 29 Stableford points were still enough for a share of sixth.
Andy Lewis: Andy Lewis played twice, in 2016 and 2017. The first ended without a card. The second brought a tied eighth at Dalmahoy, ten over, with an 88 that was fourth in the Scratch.
Roger McGuigan: Roger McGuigan finished tied twenty-first on debut at Downfield in 2024, nine over par. His second appearance, at Balmedie the following year, ended without a card.
Scott Findlay: Scott Findlay has played the last two championships, finishing nineteenth at Balmedie in 2025 and tied fifteenth at Castle Stuart in 2026, fourteen over par.
James Cannon:
James Cannon's debut at Balmedie in 2025 ended without a card, though his 29 Stableford points still earned a share of seventh.

He finished tied twenty-fifth at Castle Stuart the following year, and has brought his handicap down from 13 to 9 across the two.
Stephen Brown:
Stephen Brown has played the last two championships and picked up in both.

Even so, his 29 Stableford points at Balmedie in 2025 earned a share of seventh. In the Stableford a picked-up hole only costs you that hole, where in the Main it ends the round.
Colin Speirs:
Colin Speirs finished third at Castle Stuart in 2026 on his only appearance, six over, with an 83 that tied for second in the Scratch and 30 points for a share of third in the Stableford.

Off five, he was the best of that year's five debutants bar one, and the one was the champion, Steven Leisegang.
John Dundas:
John Dundas was tied fourth on debut at Castle Stuart in 2026, seven over, with 30 points for a share of third in the Stableford and a 91 for a share of eighth in the Scratch.

His was one of the four cards held up by the delay in group two's scoring that day, which kept him off the leaderboard for the first three hours of the championship.
Chris Merrilees:
Chris Merrilees finished twelfth at Castle Stuart in 2026 on his only appearance, twelve over, with a 92 for thirteenth in the Scratch.

He was in group two, whose scores did not reach the board until around the ninth.
Stephen McCall: Stephen McCall finished twenty-seventh at Castle Stuart in 2026 on his only appearance, with a 103.
Jamie Jordan: Jamie Jordan finished fourth at Lanark in 2015 on his only appearance, nine over, with a 93 that was fifth in the Scratch and 30 points for a share of fifth in the Stableford.
Gary Simpson: Gary Simpson finished tied fifth at Lanark in 2015 on his only appearance, ten over, and off 20 took a share of third in the Stableford with 31 points.
John Dick: John Dick finished tied seventh at Lanark in 2015 on his only appearance, eleven over, off 22. Nobody in that year's top ten played off more.
Jamie Bain: Jamie Bain finished tied tenth at Lanark in 2015 on his only appearance, sixteen over, with a 102 for a share of eighth in the Scratch.
Steven Napier: Steven Napier finished tied sixth at St Andrews in 2020 on his only appearance, eleven over, with a 99 that was eighth in the Scratch.
David Hogg: David Hogg finished twenty-sixth at Downfield in 2024 on his only appearance, fourteen over, with a 98.
Alyn Peden: Alyn Peden played one Legs Open, at Lanark in 2015, and did not return a card, though his 27 Stableford points were still good for a share of ninth.
Craig McMahon: Craig McMahon played one Legs Open, at Gullane in 2018, and did not return a card. His 22 Stableford points were seventh, in a championship where four players finished on none at all.
Sandy Hogg: Sandy Hogg played one Legs Open, at Panmure in 2023, and did not return a card. Off three, he was among the lowest handicaps in that field.
Stephen Reilly: Stephen Reilly played one Legs Open, at Balmedie in 2025, and did not return a card, though his 25 Stableford points earned a share of nineteenth.
Danny Gardiner: Danny Gardiner played one Legs Open, at St Andrews in 2020, and withdrew injured after the opening hole. Both of his two Stableford points came from that hole.
John Lyle:
John Lyle played one Legs Open, at Gullane in 2018, and finished without a point. He was one of the four in the closing group whose scorecards were destroyed by the rain, and the digital scoring failed at the same time.

None of the four returned a card, and none of them scored a point.
Paul Wright: Paul Wright played one Legs Open, at Gullane in 2018. He was in the closing group whose scorecards were ruined by the rain, with the digital backup failing alongside them, and like all four of them he finished on no points.
